verdict_label: Casual faux pas, not a major taboo
explanation: Greece does not have the strict foot taboo found in Thai/Buddhist or Gulf Arab cultures, where feet are viewed as spiritually unclean; comprehensive Greek etiquette guides do not list foot display among the country's notable taboos. That said, propping your feet on furniture or pointing the soles directly at someone is still seen as casual or mildly impolite in formal settings or someone else's home, similar to general Western manners.
local_tip: Keep your feet off tables and furniture in someone's home or in formal settings, but don't worry that an accidental foot gesture will be read as a deep insult the way it would be in Thailand.

also_check.note: Feet are considered the lowest and spiritually 'dirtiest' part of the body; showing soles or pointing feet at someone is a real insult.
Showing the soles of your feet is seen as disrespectful and implying uncleanliness.
Not a taboo, but propping feet up in formal settings can be seen as overly casual or rude.
